handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:13713:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_2_PHASE0_AUDIT_2026-04-30.md:11:**Q3 [CHALLENGE].** The accepted path is already on `transition_ledger`/`LedgerWriter`: `apply_one` canonical-encodes the `TypedTx`, CAS-puts it, builds `LedgerEntrySigningPayload`, signs it, folds `ledger_root`, commits via `writer_w.commit(&entry)`, stores `next_logical_t`, writes `q_next`, and sets `q_w.ledger_root_t` (`src/state/sequencer.rs:351`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:377`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:386`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:423`). The WorkTx shape mostly supports the validation inputs: it has `task_id`, `parent_state_root`, `agent_id`, `predicate_results`, and `stake` (`src/state/typed_tx.rs:223`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:235`), and `TypedTx` has `tx_kind()` plus `HasSubmitter::submitter_id()` rather than a `submitter_id` field (`src/state/typed_tx.rs:620`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:631`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:641`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:698`). The cascade risk is real: `EconomicState` exposes `escrows_t` and `task_markets_t`, but both are keyed by `TxId`, while `WorkTx.task_id` is a `TaskId` (`src/state/q_state.rs:143`, `src/state/q_state.rs:149`, `src/state/q_state.rs:161`, `src/state/q_state.rs:224`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:33`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:35`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:225`). A task-keyed `EscrowVault` exists, but it is separate from `QState` and explicitly "distinct from `state::q_state::EscrowEntry`" (`src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:15`, `src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:51`, `src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:53`, `src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:146`, `src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:168`). `assert_total_ctf_conserved(..., &[])` is callable, but non-empty exemptions short-circuit (`src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:167`, `src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:179`). `RejectionEvidenceWriter::append_rejected` has the named fields and is callable (`src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:258`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:268`), but `Sequencer` currently has no rejection writer field or accessor (`src/state/sequencer.rs:230`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:247`). Missing method/field finding: the preflight must specify how L4.E writer ownership and task-id-to-economic-index lookup work before Phase-1.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:13732:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R2_PRE_R3.md:26:**Finding**: No. The `CompleteSetMintTx` accept arm in `src/state/sequencer.rs:1805-1839` performs a balanced transfer. It debits `balances_t[owner]` and credits `conditional_collateral_t[event_id]` by the same `amount`. The `assert_total_ctf_conserved` invariant, extended in TB-13 to include `conditional_collateral_t` as a coin holding (`src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:186-189`), correctly verifies that this is a migration of funds, not a mint or burn. The integration test `sg_13_1_mint_one_coin_yields_one_yes_plus_one_no_total_coin_conserved` (`tests/tb_13_complete_set.rs:88`) explicitly confirms this.

handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:6:**audit_pipeline_smoke verdict.json**: PROCEED 38/0/0/3 (3 skipped = Layer H tamper stubs at FC1-N35)
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:7:**audit_pipeline_smoke replay**: byte-identical to verdict.json
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:30:**Finding**: The R3 fix to `assert_28_projection_no_autopsy_bytes` at `src/runtime/audit_assertions.rs:1483-1573` is adequate. My R2 VETO correctly identified that the original check for a raw 32-byte run was ineffective against a `serde_json` serialization of a CID as a decimal array. The new implementation now explicitly checks for both (a) the raw byte run in a `bincode` serialization and (b) the literal text of the JSON decimal array (e.g., `"[b₀,b₁,…,b₃₁]"`). This dual-check strategy, mirroring the pattern from TB-15 halt-trigger #5, robustly covers the two most plausible serialization paths for agent-visible data. While it is not a formal proof against all possible serialization formats (e.g., a custom `Debug` implementation), it directly and effectively closes the VETO-class gap. The remaining risk is sufficiently low for a Class 3 smoke test.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:38:**Finding**: The new supplemental assertion `assert_d_total_supply_conserved_per_block` (id=40) at `src/runtime/audit_assertions.rs:1199-1259` is an excellent and robust closure for my R2 challenge. The O(N²) incremental replay strategy is not merely a brute-force version of the end-to-end check; it correctly and directly verifies the invariant at every single transaction step (L4 entry). This granularity is sufficient to catch transient mint/burn events that would be missed by an end-of-chain check, including multiple transactions within the same `logical_t` window that net to zero. The implementation also correctly halts on the first replay error, ensuring it doesn't proceed with a broken state.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:46:**Finding**: The new supplemental assertion `assert_a_chain_agent_ids_sandbox_prefixed` (id=41) at `src/runtime/audit_assertions.rs:657-712` is insufficient. While it correctly closes the gap for *accepted* transactions by walking the L4 ledger, it completely ignores *rejected* transactions logged in L4.E. The architect's mandate in §7.7 is to "Halt if: ... non-sandbox funds used". An *attempt* to use non-sandbox funds, even if rejected by other predicates, constitutes a violation of the sandbox's integrity and should be detected by the audit. The `HasSubmitter` trait is not used for L4.E entries, but the `tx_payload_cid` is available, allowing for the same `TypedTx` decoding and submitter check. This is a remaining audit gap.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:49:- **RQ3 CHALLENGE**: The new sandbox-prefix assertion (id=41) fails to inspect rejected transactions in the L4.E log, leaving a gap in CR-16.7 enforcement (`src/runtime/audit_assertions.rs:657-712`).
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:55:**Finding**: The implementer's position—that the "non-sandbox funds used" HALT is an audit-time detection, not a sequencer admission gate—is architecturally consistent and defensible. The five halt conditions in architect §7.7 are listed as a parallel set. The other four (`conservation failure`, `raw log leak`, `price-as-truth`, `unresolved evidence gap`) are all implemented as audit-time assertions that operate on a completed chain. Interpreting the fifth condition in the same manner is a sound, parallel-structured reading of the spec. While a sequencer gate would be a stronger guarantee, the spec does not mandate it, and adding one would be a Class 3+/4 change. The current implementation of an audit-time HALT via Layer A assertions (#3 and the new #41) satisfies the literal requirement of the architect's directive for this Class 3 smoke test.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:63:**Finding**: The R3 fix to the file-level doc-comment in `src/runtime/audit_assertions.rs` is adequate. It now correctly and precisely delineates which layers and assertions are exercised by `FC1-N34` (`audit_tape`) versus `FC1-N35` (`audit_tape_tamper`). This resolves the specific error from R2 (misattribution of Layer H) and provides a clear traceability map for R-022 consumers. While even greater per-function granularity is theoretically possible, the current per-layer binding to the executing binary is a logical and sufficient level of detail that meets the spirit of the requirement.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_16_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-04_R3.md:104:- **RQ3 CHALLENGE**: The sandbox-prefix assertion `assert_a_chain_agent_ids_sandbox_prefixed` (id=41) at `src/runtime/audit_assertions.rs:657-712` does not check rejected transactions in the L4.E log, leaving an audit gap for CR-16.7.

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_14_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R2.md:3881:handover/tracer_bullets/TB_LOG.tsv:28:# 2026-05-02 TB-8 SHIPPED — "P3 Minimal Payout / FinalizeRewardTx (single-solver MVP; first system-emitted variant that *moves money*)". Class 3 (auth-crypto-money) full dual ship-gate audit at strategic tier (NOT degraded): Codex round-1 VETO (RQ3 smoke evidence packaging missed verifier sidecars + RQ4 duplicate Confirm denial-of-payout) → determinate-best surgical remediation under feedback_elon_mode_policy round-2 auto-execute → Codex round-2 PASS. Gemini PASS round-1 strategic-tier `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` (NOT degraded; Q1-Q5 all cleared). All user-minimum 12 requirements + all charter §5 9 ship gates + all charter §4 20 forbidden lines + all 8 deliverables (Atom 0.5 + Atoms 1-8) GREEN. cargo test --workspace = 725/0/150 (+13 net TB-8 tests vs TB-7R ship 712). 5/7 SOLVED smoke runs with chain-backed FinalizeReward + Finalized claim row + payout_micro=100,000 across 5+ distinct heldout-49 problems (mathd_algebra_171/107/359/10/11; mathd_numbertheory_961; aime_1997_p9). 2/7 UNSOLVED with no fake Finalized claim. Architectural surfaces: (a) 5→4 holding migration on monetary_invariant — claims_t becomes intent registry (not a holding) since FinalizeReward dispatches escrows→balances directly per charter Atom 3; new assert_claim_amount_backed_by_escrow + ClaimUnbacked variant enforce intent-vs-backing integrity; (b) zero-window MVP literally sets claim.challenge_window_close_logical_t=0 with gate firing only when window>0 (per ratification §1 Q3 + §2.4 namespace correction — agent-controlled verify.timestamp_logical NEVER comparable to sequencer-controlled fr.timestamp_logical); (c) one-claim-per-work_tx_id idempotency in Atom-1 writer (round-2 RQ4 fix); (d) self-contained tar.gz packaging — full runtime_repo/ + cas/ dirs, NOT just .git (round-2 RQ3 fix). Production claim adds: "TuringOS closes the 5-step compile loop's settlement node. Every accepted L4 WorkTx with closed challenge window + no upheld challenge produces exactly one L4 FinalizeRewardTx that atomically debits escrows_t + credits balances_t + flips claims_t.status=Finalized. FinalizeRewardTx is system-only (TB-5 RSP-3.0 inheritance — agent ingress rejects pre-queue). CTF conserved on a 4-holding sum (escrow -reward + balance +reward = 0 delta). Dashboard §9 TB-8 Claims surfaces claim_status + payout_amount per row with aggregate total_payout. Solver balance increases by exactly task_market.total_escrow on every chain-oracle-verified solve; the same is reconstructible from L4+CAS alone via verify_chaintape." Open follow-ups (carry-forward, NOT ship blockers): OBS-A Codex round-2 residual stale local commentary around the now-fixed duplicate-Confirm path (documentation cleanup; non-blocking); OBS-B best-effort emit Ok(false) on poll-budget expiry leaves solver owed-but-unpaid in solo-run MVP — acceptable per charter, becomes blocker once production SLA / public user wallet enters scope; OBS-1 (TB-7R carry-forward) coverage denominator PartialOk → Complete dependency. Self-audit: handover/audits/RECURSIVE_AUDIT_TB_8_2026-05-02.md.

handover/audits/CODEX_CO1_13_ROUND2_AUDIT_2026-04-29.md:4857:./handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R7.md:6385:handover/preregistration/PREREG_AMENDMENT_p0_defer_2026-04-25.md:27:**Wording correction (A8 round-1 audit, Codex finding 1)**: an earlier draft of this section claimed `p_0 = 0.10` was the *strictest possible substitute*. That was backwards. The Gate H test is `j-RR ≤ p_0`, so a SMALLER `p_0` is stricter. `0.10` is the **maximum tolerated value** the PREREG admits — i.e., the LEAST strict admissible ceiling, not the strictest. Substituting it is the equivalent of running Gate H at the weakest threshold the PREREG ever sanctioned. The substitution is *operationally permitted* (the PREREG explicitly allows up to 0.10), but it is NOT a tighter-than-original guarantee.

handover/audits/EXT_CODEX_2026-04-22.md:80:Again, the performance concern is overstated as phrased. `debit_wallet` and `credit_wallet` do perform repeated `manifest()` + `downcast_mut::<WalletTool>()` scans (`/home/zephryj/projects/turingosv4/src/bus.rs:416-437`), but those functions are not on every transaction. handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_8_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-02.md:12:The migration is architecturally sound and the right call. Treating `claims_t` as a holding while the funds simultaneously reside in `escrows_t` creates a double-spend accounting paradox during the lifecycle of an open claim. By redefining `claims_t` strictly as an intent/metadata registry and enforcing the `assert_claim_amount_backed_by_escrow` invariant, we maintain strict conservation of supply (total_supply = balances + escrows + stakes + bond) while allowing atomic, single-step settlement (escrow → balance). This perfectly mirrors the cache-vs-holding precedent established in TB-3.

handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R2_PRE_R3.md:26:**Finding**: No. The `CompleteSetMintTx` accept arm in `src/state/sequencer.rs:1805-1839` performs a balanced transfer. It debits `balances_t[owner]` and credits `conditional_collateral_t[event_id]` by the same `amount`. The `assert_total_ctf_conserved` invariant, extended in TB-13 to include `conditional_collateral_t` as a coin holding (`src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:186-189`), correctly verifies that this is a migration of funds, not a mint or burn. The integration test `sg_13_1_mint_one_coin_yields_one_yes_plus_one_no_total_coin_conserved` (`tests/tb_13_complete_set.rs:88`) explicitly confirms this.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R2_PRE_R3.md:38:**Finding**: Yes. The `total_supply_micro` function in `src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:158-192` was extended to include `conditional_collateral_t` as the 6th coin holding (alongside `balances_t`, `escrows_t`, `stakes_t`, `challenge_cases_t`, and the now-removed `claims_t` which was an intent registry). All three new typed-tx variants (`CompleteSetMintTx`, `CompleteSetRedeemTx`, `MarketSeedTx`) are balanced transfers between these holdings (`balances_t` ↔ `conditional_collateral_t`). The `assert_total_ctf_conserved` invariant is called after each transition in the integration tests (e.g., `tests/tb_13_complete_set.rs:125`), confirming the sum holds.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R2_PRE_R3.md:40:**5. Does `assert_complete_set_balanced` (MIN-semantics: `min(Σ_yes, Σ_no) == collateral`) hold after every transition?**
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R2_PRE_R3.md:42:**Finding**: Yes. The `assert_complete_set_balanced` function in `src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:278-323` correctly implements the MIN-semantics invariant. This form is robust to post-resolution redemptions where the losing side's shares become stranded (and thus `Σ_losing > collateral`). The integration tests (`sg_13_1...`, `halt_total_supply_micro_unchanged_across_mint_redeem`, `halt_complete_set_balanced_post_seed`) confirm this invariant holds after mint, seed, and redeem transitions.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R2_PRE_R3.md:76:**13. Is the MIN-semantics `assert_complete_set_balanced` invariant the right form, particularly for adversarial patterns?**

Primary enforcement: syscall-layer `EPERM` trap. **Fallback enforcement** (if syscall layer not feasible in Rust user-space without privileged sandbox): library-level write gate at the artifact-write API + path whitelist + `panic!()` abort on bypass attempt + post-write `git diff` against Trust Root paths; any non-empty diff = `panic!("TRUST_ROOT_BYPASS")` and process termination. Either primary OR fallback enforcement passing the `tests/trust_root_immutability.rs` conformance suite is sufficient for Gate B; bypass through both layers = arc BLOCKER. The PREREG accepts the fallback as equivalent strength because the conformance test is identical: simulated ArchitectAI write attempts to Trust Root paths must abort the process. |

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_2_PHASE0_AUDIT_2026-04-30.md:11:**Q3 [CHALLENGE].** The accepted path is already on `transition_ledger`/`LedgerWriter`: `apply_one` canonical-encodes the `TypedTx`, CAS-puts it, builds `LedgerEntrySigningPayload`, signs it, folds `ledger_root`, commits via `writer_w.commit(&entry)`, stores `next_logical_t`, writes `q_next`, and sets `q_w.ledger_root_t` (`src/state/sequencer.rs:351`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:377`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:386`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:423`). The WorkTx shape mostly supports the validation inputs: it has `task_id`, `parent_state_root`, `agent_id`, `predicate_results`, and `stake` (`src/state/typed_tx.rs:223`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:235`), and `TypedTx` has `tx_kind()` plus `HasSubmitter::submitter_id()` rather than a `submitter_id` field (`src/state/typed_tx.rs:620`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:631`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:641`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:698`). The cascade risk is real: `EconomicState` exposes `escrows_t` and `task_markets_t`, but both are keyed by `TxId`, while `WorkTx.task_id` is a `TaskId` (`src/state/q_state.rs:143`, `src/state/q_state.rs:149`, `src/state/q_state.rs:161`, `src/state/q_state.rs:224`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:33`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:35`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:225`). A task-keyed `EscrowVault` exists, but it is separate from `QState` and explicitly "distinct from `state::q_state::EscrowEntry`" (`src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:15`, `src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:51`, `src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:53`, `src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:146`, `src/economy/escrow_vault.rs:168`). `assert_total_ctf_conserved(..., &[])` is callable, but non-empty exemptions short-circuit (`src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:167`, `src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:179`). `RejectionEvidenceWriter::append_rejected` has the named fields and is callable (`src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:258`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:268`), but `Sequencer` currently has no rejection writer field or accessor (`src/state/sequencer.rs:230`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:247`). Missing method/field finding: the preflight must specify how L4.E writer ownership and task-id-to-economic-index lookup work before Phase-1.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_2_PHASE0_AUDIT_2026-04-30.md:17:**Q6 [PASS].** The `exempt_tx_kinds` red line is technically justified. The implementation explicitly short-circuits on any non-empty exemption list: `if !exempt_tx_kinds.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }` (`src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:177`, `src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:179`). The function docs say mints/burns are rejected unless the list is non-empty and normal agent-submitted transitions should pass `&[]` (`src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:154`, `src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:166`). Current `src/` production call sites outside the function are absent; observed non-empty usage is a unit test named `ctf_exempt_short_circuits` (`src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:320`, `src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs:328`). TB-1 integration calls pass `&[]` (`tests/tb_1_acceptance.rs:355`, `tests/tb_1_acceptance.rs:382`, `tests/tb_1_acceptance.rs:445`, `tests/tb_1_acceptance.rs:540`). Verdict: this red line prevents future regression, not existing runtime misuse.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_2_PHASE0_AUDIT_2026-04-30.md:21:**Q8 [CHALLENGE].** Adversarial sweep found four missed risks. First, rejection path atomicity is under-specified: current accepted path already writes CAS before sign/commit and can leave orphan CAS objects on later failure, while the proposed rejection path adds CAS writes plus L4.E append (`src/state/sequencer.rs:351`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:363`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:417`); current `append_rejected` is infallible and in-memory, so the immediate rollback risk is limited, but persistence semantics are deferred (`src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:30`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:34`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:258`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:268`). Second, multi-producer submit order is not specified: `fetch_add` occurs before `try_send`, and `run` processes receiver arrival order (`src/state/sequencer.rs:292`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:293`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:308`); HYPOTHESIS: submit ID monotonicity must not be used as an arrival-order guarantee under contention. Third, replay determinism requires all accept-side effects to be represented in L4/QState because `replay_full_transition` re-fetches CAS payloads, re-runs `dispatch_transition`, checks `q_next.state_root_t`, and advances `q` from `q_next` (`src/bottom_white/ledger/transition_ledger.rs:371`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/transition_ledger.rs:389`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/transition_ledger.rs:442`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/transition_ledger.rs:486`); apply_one currently ignores `_signals`, so any TB-2 signal side channel would be UNVERIFIED for replay unless ledgered or declared out of scope (`src/state/sequencer.rs:341`, `src/state/sequencer.rs:346`). Fourth, the proposed `turingosv4.worktx.accept.v1` state-root domain is not registered in source or genesis; observed genesis anchors constitution and registry roots only, while the only existing state-root toy domain is `turingosv4.l4_state_root.v1` in `AcceptedLedger` (`genesis_payload.toml:118`, `genesis_payload.toml:127`, `genesis_payload.toml:133`, `src/economy/ledger.rs:350`, `src/economy/ledger.rs:357`). This is not a charter-killer, but it should be made an explicit constant and documented as an interim domain.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_2_PHASE0_AUDIT_2026-04-30.md:31:4. **Define concrete error and rejection-class mapping.** Evidence: `TransitionError` has `StakeInsufficient`, `TaskNotFound`, and `NotYetImplemented`, but no `EscrowMissing` or `PostInitMint` variants (`src/state/typed_tx.rs:717`, `src/state/typed_tx.rs:787`). `RejectionEvidence::RejectionClass` has coarse `PredicateFailed`, `PolicyViolation`, `EscrowMissing`, and `InvariantViolation`, not the exact `StakeRequired`/`PostInitMint` names in the battery (`src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:56`, `src/bottom_white/ledger/rejection_evidence.rs:67`, `handover/ai-direct/TB-2_SEQUENCER_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_2026-04-30.md:138`, `handover/ai-direct/TB-2_SEQUENCER_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_2026-04-30.md:140`). Remediation: pre-register `TransitionError -> RejectionClass` mapping and adjust expected test names/classes, or explicitly approve new `TransitionError` variants in `typed_tx.rs`. Estimated effort: 0.25-0.5 day. Scope note: new `TransitionError` variants force an edit outside `sequencer.rs`.

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R9.md:8726:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R7.md:6385:handover/preregistration/PREREG_AMENDMENT_p0_defer_2026-04-25.md:27:**Wording correction (A8 round-1 audit, Codex finding 1)**: an earlier draft of this section claimed `p_0 = 0.10` was the *strictest possible substitute*. That was backwards. The Gate H test is `j-RR ≤ p_0`, so a SMALLER `p_0` is stricter. `0.10` is the **maximum tolerated value** the PREREG admits — i.e., the LEAST strict admissible ceiling, not the strictest. Substituting it is the equivalent of running Gate H at the weakest threshold the PREREG ever sanctioned. The substitution is *operationally permitted* (the PREREG explicitly allows up to 0.10), but it is NOT a tighter-than-original guarantee.

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R9.md:10458:handover/audits/EXT_CODEX_2026-04-22.md:80:Again, the performance concern is overstated as phrased. `debit_wallet` and `credit_wallet` do perform repeated `manifest()` + `downcast_mut::<WalletTool>()` scans (`/home/zephryj/projects/turingosv4/src/bus.rs:416-437`), but those functions are not on every transaction. handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R9.md:11664:.claude/worktrees/phase-8a-snapshot/handover/audits/EXT_CODEX_2026-04-22.md:80:Again, the performance concern is overstated as phrased. `debit_wallet` and `credit_wallet` do perform repeated `manifest()` + `downcast_mut::<WalletTool>()` scans (`/home/zephryj/projects/turingosv4/src/bus.rs:416-437`), but those functions are not on every transaction. They are used on bus-side invest/refund/hayek/settlement paths (`/home/zephryj/projects/turingosv4/src/bus.rs:233,240,346,359,383-412`), while evaluator-side invest does its own separate wallet downcasts (`/home/zephryj/projects/turingosv4/experiments/minif2f_v4/src/bin/evaluator.rs:694-716`). The deeper issue is architectural duplication and bus bypass, not the raw dynamic-dispatch cost alone.

handover/evidence/tb_8_minimal_payout_smoke_2026-05-02/README.md:86:Codex round-1 audit found that two Confirm VerifyTxs targeting the SAME WorkTx would create two Open `claims_t` rows (each backed individually by the same escrow). At finalize time, the per-claim `assert_claim_amount_backed_by_escrow` invariant would PASS individually (escrow ≥ each claim's amount), but post-mutation the escrow would drop to 0, leaving the OTHER Open claim unbacked → `MonetaryInvariantViolation` → finalize blocked. This is a denial-of-payout attack on the first money-moving system tx.

handover/architect-insights/TAPE_CANONICAL_AUDIT_2026-04-26_AUDITOR.md:19:6. **V-06 Wall-clock T_i bracket is parallel ledger**. `RunWallClock` uses `Instant` (process-monotonic, non-serialisable). `Node.created_at: u64` is **seconds resolution** (`bus.rs:264-267`); a 5-second LLM call and a 5.999-second LLM call get the same timestamp on the tape. Phase B B3 millisecond budget assertions cannot be reconstructed from tape alone.

handover/ai-direct/TB-2_SEQUENCER_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_2026-04-30.md:491:**Note on Test 6 (post-init mint via WorkTx) — DROPPED from runtime battery.** Per Codex r1 CHL-S3: WorkTx carries no economic-delta field; mint-via-WorkTx is not a representable transition. The post-init mint invariant is already proven at the primitive level by TB-1's `assert_no_post_init_mint` unit tests in `src/economy/monetary_invariant.rs::tests` and re-confirmed at runtime by I7's "no state advance on reject" property — any `q_next` that violates supply conservation would either (i) be impossible to construct (the WorkTx arm computes `q_next` itself; any path that would mint requires an attacker to supply a malformed `q_next` directly, which the runtime never accepts) or (ii) be caught by `assert_total_ctf_conserved(..., &[])` and routed to L4.E with `InvariantViolation`. If/when a future TB introduces a `TypedTx` variant that CAN carry a supply delta (e.g. RSP-2's `settlement_tx`), the runtime post-init mint test moves into THAT TB's battery.

handover/ai-direct/LATEST.md:746:"TB-13 introduces the Polymarket / CTF mathematical core (`1 locked Coin = 1 YES_E + 1 NO_E`) as a non-trading collateral + share accounting layer on top of TB-12's NodePositionsIndex substrate. CompleteSetMintTx is balance↔collateral migration with equal YES/NO claim issuance; CompleteSetRedeemTx redeems winning side post-system-resolved outcome (canonical `task_markets_t.state`); MarketSeedTx provider explicit-funds protocol-owned share inventory. Six-holding CTF (balances + escrows + stakes + challenge_cases + conditional_collateral) preserved bit-equal across all 3 typed-tx; conditional shares are claims, NOT Coin (CR-13.3 + SG-13.2). MIN-semantics `assert_complete_set_balanced` invariant called live from each dispatch arm post-mutation. Submit-time + replay-time agent signature verification (Class 3 admission control) for all 3 variants. Forward-fence (3-layer marker + type-name + hard-import discipline) prevents legacy f64 CPMM contamination. Two architect-spec deviations (`u128 ShareAmount` + `ResolutionRef` removed) endorsed by clean-room auditor as tighter-than-spec but requiring architect ratification before TB-14."

(A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).

FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R6.md:5145:- A8e2 (post-A8e, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-2 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini CHALLENGE — both convergent): three dual-audit fixes. **G1** (Codex R2#1 + Gemini R2#1) `experiments/minif2f_v4/tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` wraps `python3 scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` in a Rust integration test, making the V3L-27 round-robin conformance gate run on every `cargo test --workspace`. **G2** (Codex R2#2) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 8` audit-requirements paragraph reworded — round-1 fix corrected § 2 but left § 8 still calling the substitution a "strictest plausible bar"; now consistent across the doc. Re-hashed in Trust Root. **G3** (Codex R2#3 + Gemini R2#2) `A8_EXIT_PACKET` updated for round-2 reality: § 2 cumulative-tests table extended with A8e/A8e2 columns, § 4 manifest-clean assertion bumped 30→34, § 5 round-1 risk #5 (no FC1-N12 in swarm verify path) removed (closed by F4), § 6 Q7.a/b numbers updated, round-2 outcome + round-3 fixes section appended; TRACE_MATRIX stale `run_corr_id` symbol row replaced; "in CI" softened to "via Rust wrapper post-A8e2". FC-trace: meta governance + V3L-27 mitigation gating (FC1-N7). Trust Root manifest 33 → 34 (`tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs`).
handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R6.md:5146:- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. (A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).
handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R6.md:5195:| `tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` Rust→Python wrapper (A8e2 fix G1) | `experiments/minif2f_v4/tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` | A8 round-2 audit (Codex R2#1 + Gemini R2#1): the round-robin conformance battery in `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` was only manual; tests that don't run automatically are documentation, not gates. G1 wires the Python suite into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust integration test that shells to `python3` and asserts exit 0 + the unittest "OK" trailer. The V3L-27 mitigation (case C-027) is now a recurring conformance gate exercised on every commit that touches Rust + every CI pipeline that already exercises Rust tests. | ✅ |

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:2503:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:84:    **Finding**: **PASS (Addressed)**. Yes, the concern is fully and elegantly addressed. My previous challenge noted that coupling redemption to specific transaction types via `ResolutionRef` was brittle. By removing `ResolutionRef` and having the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` check the canonical `task_markets_t.state` enum directly, the design is now much more extensible. If a future TB introduces a new resolution mechanism (e.g., a `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`), it only needs to mutate `task_markets_t.state` to a resolved value. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` logic will not need to be changed at all. This is a significant architectural improvement.

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:3561:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:9396:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:40:**Finding**: PASS. No. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` performs a state lookup on `task_markets_t`. If the state is `Open` or `Expired`, it is correctly rejected with `RedeemBeforeResolution`. This is confirmed by integration test `sg_13_5_redeem_unavailable_before_outcome_resolution` in `tests/tb_13_complete_set.rs`.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:3565:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:9401:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:74:**Finding**: CHALLENGE. The current `ResolutionRef` model at `src/state/typed_tx.rs:1120` and its validation logic in `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` are tightly coupled to specific transaction types (`TaskBankruptcyTx`, `FinalizeRewardTx`). If TB-15+ introduces new resolution mechanisms (e.g., `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`, `OracleUpdateTx`), the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm will require modification to recognize these new transaction types. A more abstract and robust long-term design might involve a canonical `ResolutionsIndex` in `QState` that maps `EventId` to a resolved `OutcomeSide`, decoupling the redemption logic from the specific mechanism of resolution. The current implementation is not a bug but represents an architectural choice that incurs future refactoring debt.

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:4004:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:40:**Finding**: PASS. No. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` performs a state lookup on `task_markets_t`. If the state is `Open` or `Expired`, it is correctly rejected with `RedeemBeforeResolution`. This is confirmed by integration test `sg_13_5_redeem_unavailable_before_outcome_resolution` in `tests/tb_13_complete_set.rs`.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:4014:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:74:**Finding**: CHALLENGE. The current `ResolutionRef` model at `src/state/typed_tx.rs:1120` and its validation logic in `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` are tightly coupled to specific transaction types (`TaskBankruptcyTx`, `FinalizeRewardTx`). If TB-15+ introduces new resolution mechanisms (e.g., `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`, `OracleUpdateTx`), the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm will require modification to recognize these new transaction types. A more abstract and robust long-term design might involve a canonical `ResolutionsIndex` in `QState` that maps `EventId` to a resolved `OutcomeSide`, decoupling the redemption logic from the specific mechanism of resolution. The current implementation is not a bug but represents an architectural choice that incurs future refactoring debt.

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:6971:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md.raw:2503:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:84:    **Finding**: **PASS (Addressed)**. Yes, the concern is fully and elegantly addressed. My previous challenge noted that coupling redemption to specific transaction types via `ResolutionRef` was brittle. By removing `ResolutionRef` and having the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` check the canonical `task_markets_t.state` enum directly, the design is now much more extensible. If a future TB introduces a new resolution mechanism (e.g., a `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`), it only needs to mutate `task_markets_t.state` to a resolved value. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` logic will not need to be changed at all. This is a significant architectural improvement.

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:13467:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md.raw:7055:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md.raw:3565:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:9401:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:74:**Finding**: CHALLENGE. The current `ResolutionRef` model at `src/state/typed_tx.rs:1120` and its validation logic in `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` are tightly coupled to specific transaction types (`TaskBankruptcyTx`, `FinalizeRewardTx`). If TB-15+ introduces new resolution mechanisms (e.g., `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`, `OracleUpdateTx`), the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm will require modification to recognize these new transaction types. A more abstract and robust long-term design might involve a canonical `ResolutionsIndex` in `QState` that maps `EventId` to a resolved `OutcomeSide`, decoupling the redemption logic from the specific mechanism of resolution. The current implementation is not a bug but represents an architectural choice that incurs future refactoring debt.

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R4.md:5109:- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. (A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).
handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R4.md:5158:| `tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` Rust→Python wrapper (A8e2 fix G1) | `experiments/minif2f_v4/tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` | A8 round-2 audit (Codex R2#1 + Gemini R2#1): the round-robin conformance battery in `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` was only manual; tests that don't run automatically are documentation, not gates. G1 wires the Python suite into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust integration test that shells to `python3` and asserts exit 0 + the unittest "OK" trailer. handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:50:    **Finding**: **PASS**. No. The gate at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` checks `task_markets_t` for a resolved state (`Finalized` or `Bankrupt`). An `Open` or `Expired` state correctly results in a `RedeemBeforeResolution` rejection.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:84:    **Finding**: **PASS (Addressed)**. Yes, the concern is fully and elegantly addressed. My previous challenge noted that coupling redemption to specific transaction types via `ResolutionRef` was brittle. By removing `ResolutionRef` and having the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` check the canonical `task_markets_t.state` enum directly, the design is now much more extensible. If a future TB introduces a new resolution mechanism (e.g., a `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`), it only needs to mutate `task_markets_t.state` to a resolved value. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` logic will not need to be changed at all. This is a significant architectural improvement.

(A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:9396:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:40:**Finding**: PASS. No. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` performs a state lookup on `task_markets_t`. If the state is `Open` or `Expired`, it is correctly rejected with `RedeemBeforeResolution`. This is confirmed by integration test `sg_13_5_redeem_unavailable_before_outcome_resolution` in `tests/tb_13_complete_set.rs`.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:9401:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:74:**Finding**: CHALLENGE. The current `ResolutionRef` model at `src/state/typed_tx.rs:1120` and its validation logic in `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` are tightly coupled to specific transaction types (`TaskBankruptcyTx`, `FinalizeRewardTx`). If TB-15+ introduces new resolution mechanisms (e.g., `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`, `OracleUpdateTx`), the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm will require modification to recognize these new transaction types. A more abstract and robust long-term design might involve a canonical `ResolutionsIndex` in `QState` that maps `EventId` to a resolved `OutcomeSide`, decoupling the redemption logic from the specific mechanism of resolution. The current implementation is not a bug but represents an architectural choice that incurs future refactoring debt.

All user-minimum 12 requirements + all charter §5 9 ship gates + all charter §4 20 forbidden lines + all 8 deliverables (Atom 0.5 + Atoms 1-8) GREEN. cargo test --workspace = 725/0/150 (+13 net TB-8 tests vs TB-7R ship 712). 5/7 SOLVED smoke runs with chain-backed FinalizeReward + Finalized claim row + payout_micro=100,000 across 5+ distinct heldout-49 problems (mathd_algebra_171/107/359/10/11; mathd_numbertheory_961; aime_1997_p9). 2/7 UNSOLVED with no fake Finalized claim. Architectural surfaces: (a) 5→4 holding migration on monetary_invariant — claims_t becomes intent registry (not a holding) since FinalizeReward dispatches escrows→balances directly per charter Atom 3; new assert_claim_amount_backed_by_escrow + ClaimUnbacked variant enforce intent-vs-backing integrity; (b) zero-window MVP literally sets claim.challenge_window_close_logical_t=0 with gate firing only when window>0 (per ratification §1 Q3 + §2.4 namespace correction — agent-controlled verify.timestamp_logical NEVER comparable to sequencer-controlled fr.timestamp_logical); (c) one-claim-per-work_tx_id idempotency in Atom-1 writer (round-2 RQ4 fix); (d) self-contained tar.gz packaging — full runtime_repo/ + cas/ dirs, NOT just .git (round-2 RQ3 fix). Production claim adds: "TuringOS closes the 5-step compile loop's settlement node. Every accepted L4 WorkTx with closed challenge window + no upheld challenge produces exactly one L4 FinalizeRewardTx that atomically debits escrows_t + credits balances_t + flips claims_t.status=Finalized. FinalizeRewardTx is system-only (TB-5 RSP-3.0 inheritance — agent ingress rejects pre-queue). CTF conserved on a 4-holding sum (escrow -reward + balance +reward = 0 delta). Dashboard §9 TB-8 Claims surfaces claim_status + payout_amount per row with aggregate total_payout. Solver balance increases by exactly task_market.total_escrow on every chain-oracle-verified solve; the same is reconstructible from L4+CAS alone via verify_chaintape." Open follow-ups (carry-forward, NOT ship blockers): OBS-A Codex round-2 residual stale local commentary around the now-fixed duplicate-Confirm path (documentation cleanup; non-blocking); OBS-B best-effort emit Ok(false) on poll-budget expiry leaves solver owed-but-unpaid in solo-run MVP — acceptable per charter, becomes blocker once production SLA / public user wallet enters scope; OBS-1 (TB-7R carry-forward) coverage denominator PartialOk → Complete dependency. Yes, the concern is fully and elegantly addressed. My previous challenge noted that coupling redemption to specific transaction types via `ResolutionRef` was brittle. By removing `ResolutionRef` and having the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` check the canonical `task_markets_t.state` enum directly, the design is now much more extensible. If a future TB introduces a new resolution mechanism (e.g., a `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`), it only needs to mutate `task_markets_t.state` to a resolved value. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` logic will not need to be changed at all. This is a significant architectural improvement.

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R5.md:3979:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:6971:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md.raw:2503:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:84:    **Finding**: **PASS (Addressed)**. Yes, the concern is fully and elegantly addressed. My previous challenge noted that coupling redemption to specific transaction types via `ResolutionRef` was brittle. By removing `ResolutionRef` and having the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` check the canonical `task_markets_t.state` enum directly, the design is now much more extensible. If a future TB introduces a new resolution mechanism (e.g., a `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`), it only needs to mutate `task_markets_t.state` to a resolved value. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` logic will not need to be changed at all. This is a significant architectural improvement.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R5.md:4063:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:7055:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md.raw:3565:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:9401:handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:74:**Finding**: CHALLENGE. The current `ResolutionRef` model at `src/state/typed_tx.rs:1120` and its validation logic in `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` are tightly coupled to specific transaction types (`TaskBankruptcyTx`, `FinalizeRewardTx`). If TB-15+ introduces new resolution mechanisms (e.g., `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`, `OracleUpdateTx`), the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm will require modification to recognize these new transaction types. A more abstract and robust long-term design might involve a canonical `ResolutionsIndex` in `QState` that maps `EventId` to a resolved `OutcomeSide`, decoupling the redemption logic from the specific mechanism of resolution. The current implementation is not a bug but represents an architectural choice that incurs future refactoring debt.

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R5.md:4488:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md:12882:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R4.md.raw:1510:handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R2.md:4333:**RQ5 — ResolutionRef integrity**: TB-13 uses `ResolutionRef { resolution_tx_id, claimed_outcome }` but the sequencer ONLY validates the task_market state (Finalized/Bankrupt) + the claimed_outcome match. The `resolution_tx_id` is opaque traceability metadata, NOT validated against L4. Is this safe? Argument: task_markets_t.state IS the on-chain state-of-truth for resolution; resolution_tx_id is for L4-audit replay. Charge: a malicious agent could submit a CompleteSetRedeemTx with resolution_tx_id pointing to a non-existent or wrong tx. Is this a concern? Sequencer ignores resolution_tx_id at validation — only the task_market state matters. Is this the right design or a security gap?

(A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).

handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R5.md:6065:    58	    **Finding**: PASS. No. The gate at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` checks `task_markets_t` for a resolved state (`Finalized` or `Bankrupt`), correctly rejecting with `RedeemBeforeResolution` otherwise.
handover/audits/CODEX_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R5.md:6099:    92	    **Finding**: PASS (Fully Addressed). Yes. My previous challenge noted that coupling redemption to specific transaction types via `ResolutionRef` was brittle. By removing `ResolutionRef` and having the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` check the canonical `task_markets_t.state` enum directly, the design is now much more extensible and robust. If a future TB introduces a new resolution mechanism, it only needs to mutate `task_markets_t.state` to a resolved value; the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` logic will not need to be changed. This is a significant architectural improvement that makes future evolution easier.

handover/audits/CODEX_CO1_13_ROUND2_AUDIT_2026-04-29.md:4427:./handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R8.md:5410:- A8e2 (post-A8e, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-2 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini CHALLENGE — both convergent): three dual-audit fixes. **G1** (Codex R2#1 + Gemini R2#1) `experiments/minif2f_v4/tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` wraps `python3 scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` in a Rust integration test, making the V3L-27 round-robin conformance gate run on every `cargo test --workspace`. **G2** (Codex R2#2) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 8` audit-requirements paragraph reworded — round-1 fix corrected § 2 but left § 8 still calling the substitution a "strictest plausible bar"; now consistent across the doc. Re-hashed in Trust Root. **G3** (Codex R2#3 + Gemini R2#2) `A8_EXIT_PACKET` updated for round-2 reality: § 2 cumulative-tests table extended with A8e/A8e2 columns, § 4 manifest-clean assertion bumped 30→34, § 5 round-1 risk #5 (no FC1-N12 in swarm verify path) removed (closed by F4), § 6 Q7.a/b numbers updated, round-2 outcome + round-3 fixes section appended; TRACE_MATRIX stale `run_corr_id` symbol row replaced; "in CI" softened to "via Rust wrapper post-A8e2". FC-trace: meta governance + V3L-27 mitigation gating (FC1-N7). Trust Root manifest 33 → 34 (`tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs`).
handover/audits/CODEX_CO1_13_ROUND2_AUDIT_2026-04-29.md:4428:./handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R8.md:5411:- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. (A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).
handover/audits/CODEX_CO1_13_ROUND2_AUDIT_2026-04-29.md:4434:./handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R8.md:5460:| `tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` Rust→Python wrapper (A8e2 fix G1) | `experiments/minif2f_v4/tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` | A8 round-2 audit (Codex R2#1 + Gemini R2#1): the round-robin conformance battery in `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` was only manual; tests that don't run automatically are documentation, not gates. G1 wires the Python suite into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust integration test that shells to `python3` and asserts exit 0 + the unittest "OK" trailer. The V3L-27 mitigation (case C-027) is now a recurring conformance gate exercised on every commit that touches Rust + every CI pipeline that already exercises Rust tests. | ✅ |

handover/audits/CODEX_CO1_13_ROUND2_AUDIT_2026-04-29.md:5679:./handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R13.md:6795:handover/alignment/TRACE_MATRIX_v2_2026-04-25.md:27:- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. (A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).

(A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).
handover/audits/CODEX_CO1_13_ROUND2_AUDIT_2026-04-29.md:7960:./handover/alignment/TRACE_MATRIX_v2_2026-04-25.md:76:| `tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` Rust→Python wrapper (A8e2 fix G1) | `experiments/minif2f_v4/tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` | A8 round-2 audit (Codex R2#1 + Gemini R2#1): the round-robin conformance battery in `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` was only manual; tests that don't run automatically are documentation, not gates. handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:4:**Test baseline**: cargo test --workspace = 783 PASS / 0 FAILED / 150 ignored
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:40:**Finding**: PASS. No. The `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` performs a state lookup on `task_markets_t`. If the state is `Open` or `Expired`, it is correctly rejected with `RedeemBeforeResolution`. This is confirmed by integration test `sg_13_5_redeem_unavailable_before_outcome_resolution` in `tests/tb_13_complete_set.rs`.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R3.md:74:**Finding**: CHALLENGE. The current `ResolutionRef` model at `src/state/typed_tx.rs:1120` and its validation logic in `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` are tightly coupled to specific transaction types (`TaskBankruptcyTx`, `FinalizeRewardTx`). If TB-15+ introduces new resolution mechanisms (e.g., `ChallengeCourtRulingTx`, `OracleUpdateTx`), the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm will require modification to recognize these new transaction types. A more abstract and robust long-term design might involve a canonical `ResolutionsIndex` in `QState` that maps `EventId` to a resolved `OutcomeSide`, decoupling the redemption logic from the specific mechanism of resolution. The current implementation is not a bug but represents an architectural choice that incurs future refactoring debt.

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R13.md:6795:handover/alignment/TRACE_MATRIX_v2_2026-04-25.md:27:- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. (A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R13.md:11090:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R6.md:5882:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R5.md:5751:    27	**Wording correction (A8 round-1 audit, Codex finding 1)**: an earlier draft of this section claimed `p_0 = 0.10` was the *strictest possible substitute*. That was backwards. The Gate H test is `j-RR ≤ p_0`, so a SMALLER `p_0` is stricter. `0.10` is the **maximum tolerated value** the PREREG admits — i.e., the LEAST strict admissible ceiling, not the strictest. Substituting it is the equivalent of running Gate H at the weakest threshold the PREREG ever sanctioned. The substitution is *operationally permitted* (the PREREG explicitly allows up to 0.10), but it is NOT a tighter-than-original guarantee.

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R13.md:11996:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R10.md:8827:./handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R6.md:7071:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R4.md:6380:handover/audits/A8_EXIT_PACKET_2026-04-26.md:215:- (Q2.a) ~~Substituting `p_0 = 0.10` at the Gate H consumer (the PREREG § 5.5 ceiling) is described as conservative.~~ **CLOSED A8e F6 + A8e2 G2 + A8e3 H1**: the substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT conservative. No Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive (PREREG § 5.4). Wording fixed in PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2 (A8e F6) + § 8 (A8e2 G2) + this packet's A1-atom description (A8e3 H1). handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R13.md:11997:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R10.md:8828:./handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R6.md:7072:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R4.md:6381:handover/preregistration/PREREG_AMENDMENT_p0_defer_2026-04-25.md:27:**Wording correction (A8 round-1 audit, Codex finding 1)**: an earlier draft of this section claimed `p_0 = 0.10` was the *strictest possible substitute*. That was backwards. The Gate H test is `j-RR ≤ p_0`, so a SMALLER `p_0` is stricter. `0.10` is the **maximum tolerated value** the PREREG admits — i.e., the LEAST strict admissible ceiling, not the strictest. Substituting it is the equivalent of running Gate H at the weakest threshold the PREREG ever sanctioned. The substitution is *operationally permitted* (the PREREG explicitly allows up to 0.10), but it is NOT a tighter-than-original guarantee.

handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R5.md:58:    **Finding**: PASS. No. The gate at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` checks `task_markets_t` for a resolved state (`Finalized` or `Bankrupt`), correctly rejecting with `RedeemBeforeResolution` otherwise.
handover/audits/GEMINI_TB_13_SHIP_AUDIT_2026-05-03_R5.md:92:    **Finding**: PASS (Fully Addressed). Yes. My previous challenge noted that coupling redemption to specific transaction types via `ResolutionRef` was brittle. By removing `ResolutionRef` and having the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` dispatch arm at `src/state/sequencer.rs:1882` check the canonical `task_markets_t.state` enum directly, the design is now much more extensible and robust. If a future TB introduces a new resolution mechanism, it only needs to mutate `task_markets_t.state` to a resolved value; the `CompleteSetRedeemTx` logic will not need to be changed. This is a significant architectural improvement that makes future evolution easier.

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R9.md:5438:- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. (A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R9.md:7745:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R5.md:7898:    16	- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R9.md:8682:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R7.md:5278:- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. (A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).
handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R9.md:8684:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R7.md:5327:| `tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` Rust→Python wrapper (A8e2 fix G1) | `experiments/minif2f_v4/tests/llm_proxy_python_conformance.rs` | A8 round-2 audit (Codex R2#1 + Gemini R2#1): the round-robin conformance battery in `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` was only manual; tests that don't run automatically are documentation, not gates. G1 wires the Python suite into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust integration test that shells to `python3` and asserts exit 0 + the unittest "OK" trailer. The V3L-27 mitigation (case C-027) is now a recurring conformance gate exercised on every commit that touches Rust + every CI pipeline that already exercises Rust tests. | ✅ |

handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R9.md:9202:handover/audits/CODEX_PHASE_A8_EXIT_AUDIT_2026-04-26_R4.md:7661:handover/alignment/TRACE_MATRIX_v2_2026-04-25.md:15:- A8e (post-A7, FIX-THEN-PROCEED after A8 round-1 audit Codex CHALLENGE / Gemini VETO): six dual-audit fixes. **F1** (Codex#2 + Gemini Q4) `experiments/minif2f_v4/src/run_id.rs` mints one stable run_id per run, threaded into both `emit_event` and `make_pput` (replaces `run_corr_id` vs internal `run_id` ms drift; oneshot also stops using `oneshot_{problem_file}` placeholder). **F2** (Gemini VETO Q6) `scripts/test_llm_proxy.py` adds 15-test conformance battery — round-robin distributes [2,2,2] across 6 calls, single-key pool degrades to all-zero, two-key pool alternates [2,2]; exercises the V3L-27 mitigation without a live API. (A8e2 G1 wires this into `cargo test --workspace` via a Rust shell-out wrapper — see § 2 below.) **F3** (Codex#4) routing matrix bug fixed — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` was misrouting to DashScope because `m.startswith("qwen")` won after the slash check; now slash-form ⇒ siliconflow first, bare-qwen ⇒ dashscope second. **F4** (Codex#3) FC1-N12 emit added to all 3 swarm verify sites (`verify_omega_detailed` × 2 + `verify_partial`), each with verdict + elapsed_ms + path stamp; closes the swarm-side gap in the 5-step compile-loop witness. **F5** (Codex#5) `genesis_payload.toml` header + TRACE_MATRIX milestones reconciled to actual 31 entries (round-1 packet undercounted by 1 — agent_models.rs from A3 was already in TR before A1). **F6** (Codex#1) `PREREG_AMENDMENT § 2` wording corrected — `p_0=0.10` substitution is the LEAST-strict admissible ceiling (max tolerated value for `j-RR ≤ p_0`), NOT the strictest possible substitute as round-1 mistakenly claimed; explicit statistical-implications paragraph added (no Type-I inflation since `j-RR` is descriptive; substitution may be less protective than eventual calibrated `p_0 < 0.10`). FC-trace: FC1-N12 (oracle scope swarm coverage) + FC1-N7 (δ provider routing) + Art. V (amendment governance). Trust Root manifest 31 → 33 (run_id.rs + test_llm_proxy.py).

     1	//! TB-16 Atom 3 — `audit_tape` CLI (architect §7.5 + design §6).
     2	//!
     3	//! Pure audit-from-tape binary. Reads ONLY on-disk artifacts:
     4	//!   - runtime_repo/ (Git2 L4 chain + L4.E rejections.jsonl)
     5	//!   - cas/ (CAS store)
     6	//!   - agent_pubkeys.json + pinned_pubkeys.json (per-run manifests)
     7	//!   - genesis_payload.toml + constitution.md
     8	//!   - LATEST_MARKOV_CAPSULE.txt (Markov pointer)
     9	//!   - [optional] handover/alignment/ (OBS scan)
    10	//!
    11	//! NEVER reads:
    12	//!   - live Sequencer state
    13	//!   - state.db (whitebox cache; auditor rebuilds via replay_full_transition)
    14	//!   - process logs
    15	//!   - handover/ai-direct/
    16	//!
    17	//! Emits verdict.json per design §6.3 schema (38 assertions × 8 layers,
    18	//! tape_root, tx_kind_counts, feature_coverage, verdict ∈ {PROCEED, BLOCK}).
    19	//!
    20	//! Usage:
    21	//!   audit_tape \
    22	//!     --runtime-repo  <path> \
    23	//!     --cas-dir       <path> \
    24	//!     --agent-pubkeys <path> \
    25	//!     --pinned-pubkeys <path> \
    26	//!     --genesis       <path> \
    27	//!     --constitution  <path> \
    28	//!     --markov-pointer <path> \
    29	//!     [--alignment-dir <path>] \
    30	//!     --out <verdict.json>
    31	//!
    32	//! Exit code:
    33	//!   0  — verdict.json verdict == "PROCEED"
    34	//!   1  — verdict.json verdict == "BLOCK" (≥1 fail/halt)
    35	//!   2  — invalid args / I/O failure before audit could begin
    36	//!
    37	//! TRACE_MATRIX FC1-N34 (audit_tape binary) + FC2-N31 (verdict.json schema v1).

    53	    markov_pointer: PathBuf,
    54	    alignment_dir: Option<PathBuf>,

    72	                i += 1;

    74	            }
    75	            "--cas-dir" => {
    76	                i += 1;
    77	                cas_dir = Some(argv.get(i).ok_or("--cas-dir needs path")?.into());
    78	            }
    79	            "--agent-pubkeys" => {

    82	            }
    83	            "--pinned-pubkeys" => {
    84	                i += 1;
    85	                pinned_pubkeys = Some(argv.get(i).ok_or("--pinned-pubkeys needs path")?.into());
    86	            }
    87	            "--genesis" => {

    93	                constitution = Some(argv.get(i).ok_or("--constitution needs path")?.into());
    94	            }
    95	            "--markov-pointer" => {
    96	                i += 1;
    97	                markov_pointer = Some(argv.get(i).ok_or("--markov-pointer needs path")?.into());
    98	            }
    99	            "--alignment-dir" => {
   100	                i += 1;

   102	            }

   116	        runtime_repo: runtime_repo.ok_or("--runtime-repo required")?,
   117	        cas_dir: cas_dir.ok_or("--cas-dir required")?,

   119	        pinned_pubkeys: pinned_pubkeys.ok_or("--pinned-pubkeys required")?,
   120	        genesis: genesis.ok_or("--genesis required")?,

   125	    })
   126	}
